name: Lincoln Yards (northern parcel now rebranded 'Foundry Park')
current_value: For Foundry Park: developers are reported to contribute directly about $33M while roughly $202M of an estimated ~$235M in infrastructure costs (roads, parks, public improvements) would be reimbursed via TIF; a June 2026 Block Club Chicago report and CoStar separately cite more than $200M in public funding lined up for the project.
proposed_value: UPDATE: Phase 1 groundbreaking occurred as scheduled on Oct. 21, 2026 (Mayor Johnson and Kayne Anderson's David Selznick attended) on the former Finkl Steel site -- resolving the prior sweep's flagged risk that it might slip to November. No new dollar figure; the $201.6M TIF / ~$235M total figures above are unchanged.
note: 2+ source confirmed (Sun-Times, Crain's, Bisnow, Construction Review Online). Status/milestone only -- no change to announced_investment_usd ($3B).

name: Chicago Bears Stadium Proposal (formerly lakefront/Arlington Heights, now Hammond, IN)
current_value: $5 billion is the total development figure (domed stadium plus surrounding mixed-use district) reported June 2026 for the Hammond, IN project, with the Bears committing roughly $2B in private capital and Indiana authorizing legislation for up to $1B in state/local incentives. Independently confirmed via fresh searches: NFL.com, Front Office Sports, Yahoo/ESPN (Schefter), NPR Illinois, and the Sun-
proposed_value: Unsolicited third-party concept, not a site or financing change to the Hammond project above: on Oct 28, 2026, architecture firm SOM released conceptual renderings for a domed Bears stadium at the Rate Field/Bridgeport site in Chicago, contingent on the White Sox relocating to the proposed 'Railyards' site. The Bears have not endorsed this concept and publicly maintain Hammond, IN remains their sole focus; Ald. Nicole Lee (11th) said she has had no contact with the team about it. WBEZ's own framing is that both this concept and the White Sox Railyards plan have, so far, 'gone nowhere.' The $5B/Hammond figures above are unchanged.
note: 2+ source confirmed that the renderings/announcement occurred; single-source/no confirmation of any real Bears plan change. No site, status_2026, or dollar-figure change proposed for the Hammond row. Also relevant to the separate White Sox 'Railyards' project row: no change proposed there either -- WBEZ's Oct 28 characterization that Railyards has 'gone nowhere' since the Sept 5-9, 2026 announcement reconfirms no-change rather than indicating a new development.
